sections.normalized_html: The function [MATH: g] is defined by [MATH: g(x) = 5(3)^x - 7.] What is the [MATH: y]-intercept of the graph of [MATH: y = g(x)] in the [MATH: xy]-plane?

sections.normalized_html:
To find the [MATH: y]-intercept of the graph of a function, we evaluate the function at [MATH: x = 0.]

Substituting [MATH: x = 0] into the equation, we get: [MATH: g(x)|= 5(3)^{x} − 7; g(0)|= 5(3)^{0} − 7; = 5(1) − 7; = 5 − 7; = − 2]

Therefore, the [MATH: y]-intercept is the point [MATH: (0, -2).]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the exponential function [MATH: p(x) = 24 \cdot 3^x.]

We evaluate [MATH: p(x)] at three different [MATH: x]-values.

  • When [MATH: x = -1,] we have

[MATH: p(− 1)|= 24 ⋅ 3^{− 1}; = 24 ⋅ (1)/(3); = 8.]

  • When [MATH: x = 0,] we have

[MATH: p(0)|= 24 ⋅ 3^{0}; = 24 ⋅ 1; = 24.]

  • When [MATH: x = 1,] we have

[MATH: p(1)|= 24 ⋅ 3^{1}; = 24 ⋅ 3; = 72.]

So, the table that matches the function is the following:

[MATH: p(x)]

[MATH: -1]

[MATH: 8]

[MATH: 0]

[MATH: 24]

[MATH: 1]

[MATH: 72]

items.title: Identifying a Graph of an Exponential Function

sections.normalized_html: Which of the graphs above shows the function [MATH: y = 6\left(3^{x}\right)?]
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/46a1fa7dbafef50f2ea8cd5393eadc8b]

Which of the graphs above shows the function [MATH: y = 6\left(3^{x}\right)?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are given the exponential function
[MATH: y = 6 \left(3^{x}\right).]

Let's analyze the properties of this function:

  • Since the base of the exponential is [MATH: 3 > 1], the function is increasing and [MATH: y] grows rapidly as [MATH: x \to \infty.]

  • The coefficient [MATH: 6] vertically stretches the graph and makes it pass through the point [MATH: (0,6).]

  • As [MATH: x \to -\infty], [MATH: y \to 0], so the graph approaches the horizontal asymptote [MATH: y = 0.]

Additionally, note that from the given equation, we have: [MATH: y(1) = 6 \cdot 3^1 = 18 \quad\text{and}\quad y(2) = 6 \cdot 3^2 = 54] So, the graph contains the points [MATH: (1, 18)] and [MATH: (2, 54).]

Therefore, the graph that satisfies all of these properties is the following (top-left in the original picture).

Please note that the following (bottom-right in the original picture) cannot be the correct answer, since it clearly does not pass through the point [MATH: (2,54).]

Explanation:
We are given the exponential function
[MATH: y = 6 \left(3^{x}\right).]

Let's analyze the properties of this function:

- Since the base of the exponential is [MATH: 3 > 1], the function is increasing and [MATH: y] grows rapidly as [MATH: x \to \infty.]
- The coefficient [MATH: 6] vertically stretches the graph and makes it pass through the point [MATH: (0,6).]
- As [MATH: x \to -\infty], [MATH: y \to 0], so the graph approaches the horizontal asymptote [MATH: y = 0.]

Additionally, note that from the given equation, we have:
[MATH: y(1) = 6 \cdot 3^1 = 18 \quad\text{and}\quad y(2) = 6 \cdot 3^2 = 54]
So, the graph contains the points [MATH: (1, 18)] and [MATH: (2, 54).]
